sources.name: Craft Yarn Council Crochet Abbreviations Master List
Craft Yarn Council Crochet Chart Symbols

stitches.name: chain stitch
stitches.vernacular: Used for foundation chains, turning chains, chain spaces, picots, and decorative openings.
stitches.instruction: Yarn over and pull through the loop on the hook.

stitches.name: slip stitch
stitches.vernacular: Often used for joins, edging, surface crochet, and moving across stitches without adding height.
stitches.instruction: Insert hook, yarn over, and pull through the stitch and the loop on the hook.

stitches.name: single crochet
stitches.vernacular: Dense, short stitch used heavily in amigurumi, blankets, bags, and firm fabrics.
stitches.instruction: Insert hook, yarn over and pull up a loop, yarn over and pull through both loops.

stitches.name: half double crochet
stitches.vernacular: A medium-height stitch with a slightly ridged texture; useful for soft but sturdy fabric.
stitches.instruction: Yarn over, insert hook, yarn over and pull up a loop, yarn over and pull through all three loops.

stitches.name: double crochet
stitches.vernacular: Common taller stitch for blankets, garments, granny squares, mesh, and open fabrics.
stitches.instruction: Yarn over, insert hook, yarn over and pull up a loop, yarn over and pull through two loops twice.

stitches.name: treble crochet
stitches.vernacular: A tall, open stitch. Some patterns say tc or triple crochet, but tr is the CYC standard abbreviation.
stitches.instruction: Yarn over twice, insert hook, yarn over and pull up a loop, then yarn over and pull through two loops three times.

stitches.name: double treble crochet
stitches.vernacular: Very tall stitch used for lace, dramatic texture, and fast height.
stitches.instruction: Yarn over three times, insert hook, yarn over and pull up a loop, then yarn over and pull through two loops four times.

stitches.name: triple treble crochet
stitches.vernacular: Extra-tall stitch for lace, extended height, and decorative shaping.
stitches.instruction: Yarn over four times, insert hook, yarn over and pull up a loop, then yarn over and pull through two loops five times.

stitches.name: extended single crochet
stitches.chartSymbol: single crochet symbol with extension mark
stitches.vernacular: A slightly taller, more flexible single crochet variation.
stitches.instruction: Insert hook, yarn over and pull up a loop, yarn over and pull through one loop, yarn over and pull through both loops.

stitches.name: extended half double crochet
stitches.chartSymbol: half double crochet symbol with extension mark
stitches.vernacular: A taller, looser version of half double crochet.
stitches.instruction: Yarn over, insert hook, yarn over and pull up a loop, yarn over and pull through one loop, yarn over and pull through all three loops.

stitches.name: extended double crochet
stitches.chartSymbol: double crochet symbol with extension mark
stitches.vernacular: Adds height and drape compared with standard double crochet.
stitches.instruction: Yarn over, insert hook, yarn over and pull up a loop, yarn over and pull through one loop, then yarn over and pull through two loops twice.

stitches.name: extended treble crochet
stitches.chartSymbol: treble crochet symbol with extension mark
stitches.vernacular: A tall, drapey variation for open fabrics and lace effects.
stitches.instruction: Yarn over twice, insert hook, yarn over and pull up a loop, yarn over and pull through one loop, then yarn over and pull through two loops three times.

stitches.name: single crochet increase
stitches.chartSymbol: two sc symbols worked into one base
stitches.vernacular: Usually means working two stitches into the same stitch unless the pattern defines otherwise.
stitches.instruction: Work two single crochet stitches into the same stitch or space.

stitches.name: single crochet two together
stitches.chartSymbol: two sc symbols joined at top
stitches.vernacular: A common decrease; in amigurumi, inv-dec is often used for a less visible version.
stitches.instruction: Insert hook in next stitch and pull up a loop, insert hook in following stitch and pull up a loop, yarn over and pull through all loops.

stitches.name: half double crochet two together
stitches.chartSymbol: two hdc symbols joined at top
stitches.vernacular: Used to shape fabric while keeping hdc texture.
stitches.instruction: Yarn over, pull up loops in each of the next two stitches, yarn over and pull through all loops.

stitches.name: double crochet two together
stitches.chartSymbol: two dc symbols joined at top
stitches.vernacular: Common shaping decrease in garments, blankets, and lace.
stitches.instruction: Work two partial double crochet stitches over the next two stitches, then yarn over and pull through all remaining loops.

stitches.name: treble crochet two together
stitches.chartSymbol: two tr symbols joined at top
stitches.vernacular: Tall decrease used in lace, shaping, and decorative motifs.
stitches.instruction: Work two partial treble crochet stitches over the next two stitches, then yarn over and pull through all remaining loops.

stitches.name: single crochet three together
stitches.chartSymbol: three sc symbols joined at top
stitches.vernacular: A stronger decrease that turns three stitches into one.
stitches.instruction: Pull up a loop in each of the next three stitches, yarn over and pull through all loops.

stitches.name: double crochet three together
stitches.chartSymbol: three dc symbols joined at top
stitches.vernacular: Can be a shaping decrease or a cluster-style texture depending on placement.
stitches.instruction: Work three partial double crochet stitches, then yarn over and pull through all remaining loops.

stitches.name: cluster
stitches.chartSymbol: multiple partial stitches joined at top
stitches.vernacular: A group of partial stitches closed together; exact stitch count should be defined by the pattern.
stitches.instruction: Work the stated number of partial stitches, then close them together at the top.

stitches.name: shell
stitches.chartSymbol: fan of stitches worked into one base
stitches.vernacular: Several stitches worked into the same stitch or space to create a fan shape.
stitches.instruction: Work the stated group of stitches into the same stitch or space.

stitches.name: V-stitch
stitches.chartSymbol: two tall stitches separated by a chain space
stitches.vernacular: Usually written as dc, ch 1, dc in the same stitch or space, but pattern definitions vary.
stitches.instruction: Work the defined stitch, chain space, and matching stitch into the same stitch or space.

stitches.name: puff stitch
stitches.vernacular: Soft raised stitch made from multiple yarn overs pulled up to the same height.
stitches.instruction: Pull up multiple tall loops in the same stitch or space, yarn over and pull through them together as directed.

stitches.name: bobble
stitches.vernacular: Raised bump usually made from several partial stitches in one place.
stitches.instruction: Work the stated number of partial stitches in one stitch, then close them together.

stitches.name: popcorn stitch
stitches.vernacular: Raised stitch often made by removing the hook and joining the first and last stitches of a group.
stitches.instruction: Work the stated group of stitches, remove hook, insert into first stitch of group, pick up loop, and pull through.

stitches.name: picot
stitches.vernacular: Tiny decorative point often used on lace edges.
stitches.instruction: Chain the stated number, then slip stitch as directed to form a small loop.

stitches.name: front post double crochet
stitches.chartSymbol: dc symbol hooked around post from front
stitches.vernacular: Worked around the post of a stitch from front to back; used for ribbing, cables, and texture.
stitches.instruction: Yarn over, insert hook from front to back to front around the post, and complete a double crochet.

stitches.name: back post double crochet
stitches.chartSymbol: dc symbol hooked around post from back
stitches.vernacular: Worked around the post of a stitch from back to front; often alternated with FPdc for ribbing.
stitches.instruction: Yarn over, insert hook from back to front to back around the post, and complete a double crochet.

stitches.name: back loop only
stitches.chartSymbol: bar at base of worked stitch
stitches.vernacular: A placement modifier, not a full stitch by itself; creates ribbing or a visible front ridge.
stitches.instruction: Work the indicated stitch through the back loop only.

stitches.name: front loop only
stitches.chartSymbol: front-loop mark at base of worked stitch
stitches.vernacular: A placement modifier, not a full stitch by itself; leaves the back loop unworked.
stitches.instruction: Work the indicated stitch through the front loop only.

stitches.name: magic ring
stitches.vernacular: Common amigurumi and motif start that pulls closed tightly.
stitches.instruction: Make an adjustable loop, work the first round into the loop, then pull the tail to close.

stitches.name: turning chain
stitches.vernacular: Chains made at the beginning of a row to reach the height of the next row.
stitches.instruction: Chain the number required for the next stitch height, then turn as directed.

stitches.name: chain space
stitches.vernacular: A space created by chains in a previous row or round; patterns often say work into ch-1 sp.
stitches.instruction: Work into the space made by the chain stitches rather than into an individual chain.

stitches.name: Tunisian simple stitch
stitches.vernacular: The foundational Tunisian stitch, worked by picking up vertical bars on the forward pass.
stitches.instruction: Insert hook under the next vertical bar, yarn over, and pull up a loop.

stitches.name: Tunisian knit stitch
stitches.vernacular: Tunisian stitch that resembles knitted stockinette on the front.
stitches.instruction: Insert hook between the front and back vertical bars, yarn over, and pull up a loop.

stitches.name: Tunisian purl stitch
stitches.vernacular: Creates a purl-like bump on Tunisian fabric.
stitches.instruction: Bring yarn to front, insert hook under the next vertical bar, yarn over, and pull up a loop.

stitches.name: Tunisian full stitch
stitches.vernacular: Picked up in the space between Tunisian stitches; often used for soft, dense texture.
stitches.instruction: Insert hook into the space between vertical bars, yarn over, and pull up a loop.

stitches.name: forward pass
stitches.vernacular: The Tunisian pass where loops are picked up and kept on the hook.
stitches.instruction: Work across the row picking up loops as directed.

stitches.name: return pass
stitches.vernacular: The Tunisian pass where loops are worked off the hook.
stitches.instruction: Yarn over and pull through loops as directed to work back across the row.
